# Hybrid Cryptography Approaches

Covers combining classical and post-quantum algorithms during the transition
period. See [citations.md](../citations.md) for full source details.

## Rationale for Hybrid Approaches

Hybrid schemes combine a classical algorithm (e.g., X25519, ECDSA) with a
post-quantum algorithm (e.g., ML-KEM, ML-DSA). Security holds as long as
**at least one** component algorithm remains unbroken [16][49].

Three factors drive hybrid adoption:

1. **HNDL protection:** Data encrypted today may be decrypted by future quantum
   computers. Hybrid key exchange provides PQ protection immediately while
   maintaining classical security [22].

2. **PQC algorithm maturity:** Two NIST Round 3 candidates (Rainbow, SIKE) were
   completely broken in 2022, demonstrating risk of sole reliance on new
   algorithms [9][26][27].

3. **Transition pragmatism:** Pure PQ deployment requires ecosystem-wide readiness.
   Hybrid provides quantum resistance without breaking backward compatibility
   during the transition [10].

**NSA position:** Hybrids are a temporary measure; the target is single-algorithm
(PQ-only) by 2035 [11][40].

**NCSC position:** Hybrid enables "traditional PKC and PQC to co-exist for a
while" but completing migration requires PKI migration to PQC certificates [10].

## Standardized Terminology

RFC 9794 (June 2025) defines the official terminology [17]:

- **PQ/T Hybrid Scheme:** Multi-algorithm construction with at least one PQ and
  one traditional algorithm
- **Component Scheme:** Individual algorithm within a hybrid
- **PQ/T Hybrid Composite:** Variant exposing components as a singular interface

## Hybrid Key Exchange (TLS 1.3)

### IETF Draft: ECDHE-MLKEM (draft-04)

The primary standard for hybrid TLS key exchange [15]:

| Combination | Client Share Size | Components |
|-------------|------------------|------------|
| X25519MLKEM768 | 1,216 bytes | 1,184 (ML-KEM-768) + 32 (X25519) |
| SecP256r1MLKEM768 | 1,249 bytes | 1,184 (ML-KEM-768) + 65 (P-256) |
| SecP384r1MLKEM1024 | 1,665 bytes | 1,568 (ML-KEM-1024) + 97 (P-384) |

Authors: Kwiatkowski (PQShield), Kampanakis (AWS), Westerbaan (Cloudflare),
Stebila (University of Waterloo). In RFC Editor Queue as of February 2026 [15].

### Deployment Status

| Implementer | Hybrid Scheme | Since |
|-------------|---------------|-------|
| Chrome | X25519MLKEM768 | March 2024 (desktop default) [20] |
| Firefox | X25519MLKEM768 | November 2024 (desktop default) [20] |
| Safari | X25519MLKEM768 | October 2025 (iOS/macOS 26) [20] |
| Go 1.24 | X25519MLKEM768 | February 2025 (default) [22][43] |
| OpenSSL 3.5 | X25519MLKEM768 | April 2025 (default TLS group) [21] |
| Cloudflare | X25519MLKEM768 | October 2022 (server-side) [20][45] |
| Kubernetes | X25519MLKEM768 | v1.33, April 2025 (via Go 1.24) [22] |

As of October 2025, 50%+ of human-initiated Cloudflare traffic uses hybrid
PQ encryption [20].

### Deployment Challenges

- **Protocol ossification:** Larger ClientHello messages (~3 kB vs 64 bytes)
  broke ~0.05% of connections due to middleboxes assuming messages fit in single
  packets [20]
- **Handshake latency:** OpenSSL reports increase from 13ms to 15.5ms with hybrid
  ML-KEM [21]

## Hybrid Key Exchange (VPN/IPsec)

### RFC 9370 — Multiple Key Exchanges in IKEv2

Published May 2023 [16]. Enables up to 7 additional key exchanges beyond the
initial one (Transform Types ADDKE1-ADDKE7, values 6-12). Key exchanges occur
in ordered IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchanges after IKE_SA_INIT.

"The final shared secret is computed from all of the component key exchange
secrets" — overall security at least as strong as each individual primitive [16].

## Hybrid Digital Signatures

### Composite ML-DSA for X.509 (draft-15)

draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-sigs defines 18 composite signature combinations
for X.509 PKI [18]:

- **ML-DSA-44** paired with: RSA-2048 (PSS/PKCS#1), Ed25519, ECDSA P-256
- **ML-DSA-65** paired with: RSA-3072/4096, ECDSA P-256/P-384/brainpool, Ed25519
- **ML-DSA-87** paired with: ECDSA P-384/P-521/brainpool, Ed448, RSA-3072/4096

A composite signature is valid only if **both** components verify [18]. The draft
has been submitted to IESG and had SECDIR/GENART reviews [18].

### General Framework

draft-ietf-tls-hybrid-design provides the general framework for hybrid key
exchange in TLS 1.3, with the security goal that the exchange is protected "if
one algorithm remains unbroken" [49].

## Notable Hybrid Deployments

### Apple iMessage PQ3

Launched February 2024 (iOS 17.4) [19]. Apple's security level framework:

| Level | Description | Example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| 0 | No E2E encryption by default | — |
| 1 | E2E encryption, no quantum protection | Most messengers |
| 2 | PQC for initial key establishment only | Signal (PQXDH) |
| 3 | PQC for both initial keys AND ongoing exchange | iMessage PQ3 |

PQ3 uses Kyber-1024 + P-256 for initial key establishment, with Kyber-768
rekeying approximately every 50 messages and guaranteed rekeying every 7 days [19].
Formal verification by two independent cryptographers confirmed protocol
security [19].

## Key Combiner Functions

Hash-based KEM combiners (draft-ounsworth-cfrg-kem-combiners-05) specify
Keccak-based combiner compatible with NIST SP 800-56Cr2, providing CCA-security
as long as at least one ingredient KEM is secure.

Dual-PRF construction based on HKDF provides security unless "extremely strong
attacks against the hash function are discovered."

## Transition Path: Hybrid → PQ-Only

The consensus path [10][11]:

1. **Now → 2027:** Deploy hybrid (classical + PQ) for key exchange
2. **2027 → 2033:** Migrate PKI to PQ certificates (composite or pure PQ)
3. **By 2035:** Drop classical components; PQ-only

This requires **two transitions** — adding PQ crypto, then removing classical —
which doubles migration complexity and requires crypto-agility from the start [10].

## Gaps and Limitations

- Composite signature standardization (6+ years in IETF) indicates complexity;
  18 combinations may fragment implementations
- No published interoperability testing results between major hybrid implementations
  (e.g., OpenSSL 3.5 ↔ BoringSSL ↔ AWS-LC)
- KEM combiner security proofs are in academic papers not fully extracted in this
  research
- The "hybrid → PQ-only" transition plan assumes PQC algorithms remain unbroken
  through 2035; a break would require different mitigation
- Downgrade attack protections are implementation-specific; Cloudflare plans
  "PQC only" mode for summer 2026
